messages.author: 7eed7eee7dd92cf3
messages.subject: categorical covariates for detection
parts:
Hi again 😁, 

I am trying to use the communityModel function for building an Occupancy model, but I can't include one categorical covariate (2 levels) in the either detCovsObservation or detCovs lists. 

Error in communityModel(data_list, model = "Occupancy", occuCovs = l
 |ist(ranef = c("ele",  :
Detection covariate  breeding is not a factor

Below the code I am using for preparing the data

area <- mysites$myarea
elevation <- mysites$altitudine
mydays <- as.integer(mydet.def$ndays.fby)
areaS <- wiqid::standardize(log(area))
eleS <- wiqid::standardize(elevation)
daysS<- wiqid::standardize(mydays)
type <- factor(mysites$type.site)
breedingF <- factor(mydet.def$breeding)
breedingFM <- matrix(factor(mydet.def$breeding))# see further comment

sitecovs <- data.frame(area=areaS,ele=eleS,type=type)

data_list <- list(ylist    = ylist,
siteCovs = sitecovs,
obsCovs  = list(effort = DetHist_list[[1]]$effort,ndays=daysS,breeding=breedingF)
)

mod.jags <- communityModel(data_list,
model="Occupancy",
occuCovs = list(ranef = c("ele","area","type")),
detCovsObservation = list(fixed = "effort",ranef=c("breeding","ndays")),
intercepts = list(det = "ranef", occu = "ranef"),
modelFile = modelfile1)

I have found this bit in the help section (detCovsObservation) for this function:
categorical must be coded as character matrix

And that is why I have tried with breedingFM, but it is not working as well. 
A matrix to me is a 2d dimension object,  but I am providing it as a vector instead.

Once I removed the breeding covariate, the function works fine.
Any help would in understanding what I am doing wrong would be appreciate. 

Stef

PS: I am using camtrapR version from github

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] categorical covariates for detection
parts:
Hi, 
As you said, categorical site-occasion covariates must be provided as character matrices. This is because there are no factor matrices in R. The vector will not work. 

To better understand the problem please share the output of 
str(breedingFM)

The problem with this line 
breedingFM <- matrix(factor(mydet.def$breeding))
Is that it will return a matrix with one column by default since ncol and nrow are not defined. If nothing else that's a dimension mismatch with the detection and effort matrix. 

Based on the error I suspect the data type may also not be correct, but I can be sure without the str() requested above.

Please also  try the example in the vignette you were referring to to see the required data structure. In the example it is a 30 rows x 5 columns matrix.
str(input_AHM$obsCovs$wind_categ)
##  chr [1:30, 1:5] "calm" "calm" "windy" "windy" "calm" "calm" "windy" "calm" ...

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] categorical covariates for detection
parts:
Hi Jurgen, 

thank you for your fast reply which is confirming my mistake. 

This factor (breeding with 2 levels) is actually a species x site x observation factor, not a "simple" site x observation factor. 

At this moment, the only idea I have to test this potential effect on the detection is to run two models, one for each level of this factor, but I don't think this is the optimal solution.

May be a multi stage occupancy model is what I need if I want to include this factor in a single multi-species occupancy model.

I greatly appreciate your support.

Stef

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] categorical covariates for detection
parts:
I'm sorry to disappoint, what you are asking is currently not implemented and not possible out of the box with communityModel. A possible solution is to modify the JAGS code to add the species index to the breeding covariate, and provide the breeding covariate as a 3-dimensional array in the input data list. 
So basically using the code the function provides as a starting point for further modifications. I believe that would be a better solution than the other suggestions. But then the predict and plot methods won't work and would also need to be adapted, which is not trivial.
I'm sorry, there are just so many possibilities with JAGS that this convenience function cannot cover all use cases. Maybe the function will allow more functionalities over time.
Best,
Jürgen
